reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of Hebrew people freely expressing their views without discouragement. The sons of the prophets openly ask questions ('Do you know that the LORD is taking your master away?'), the men of the city freely present their grievances about the water quality and barren land, messengers openly deliver messages between the king and Elijah, and even young men openly mock Elisha (though they face severe consequences for that specific action). The narrative shows no systemic discouragement of speech; rather, it depicts people - prophets, citizens, and servants - voluntarily voicing their concerns, knowledge, and questions throughout these events.
